root_causes.description: Checkout's server-side latency is saturated at the 10s histogram ceiling for the entire window (p50=p95=p99=10000ms) while its error rate stays near baseline (mean 0.004, max 0.019). This is a latency regression, not an error/abort fault, despite the HighErrorRate alert name.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.004, p95=0.015, max=0.019 (no error spike)

root_causes.description: The frontend entry point shows p99 pegged at the 10s ceiling and all sampled user journeys (browse, add-to-cart, checkout) run 15–30s with zero errors, inheriting and propagating the slowdown seen in checkout.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.008, max=0.038 (no meaningful error spike)

root_causes.description: No service exhibited an error spike or pod restart/OOM events, yet multi-second stalls appear across browse, cart and checkout journeys, suggesting a shared downstream dependency or injected fault (e.g. flag-driven) rather than a single crashing service.

evidence.observed_value: 20 traces, 0 with errors, p95_duration=46512ms; user_checkout_single=30006ms, user_add_to_cart=15005ms, user_browse_product=15000ms
evidence.expected_baseline: p95 duration < 1s, 0 errors only when healthy

remediation_steps: Break down checkout server spans by child dependency (cart, payment, shipping, currency, product-catalog, email) to locate the internal call adding multi-second latency.
Inspect flagd feature-flag configuration active during the window and disable any latency/fault injection flag affecting checkout and frontend.

Check pod CPU throttling and GC pauses for checkout and frontend (cpu ~0.025 and memory ~38MB look normal, no restarts), indicating an application/network-level induced latency rather than resource exhaustion.
Roll back or restart the degraded checkout/frontend deployment once the inducing call is identified, and add a p99 latency alert since the HighErrorRate alert masked a latency-only fault.
